subject: Clarify data lifecycle for interactive sessions & exported artifacts
messages:
From: Laura Chang <laura.chang@atlaspay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2029-10-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify data lifecycle for interactive sessions & exported artifacts

Hannah —

Quick question for our compliance board: when AtlasPay uses Redwood-hosted inference (hosted API tier), what exactly do you keep by default for interactive sessions? We need an itemized answer we can publish internally that covers:
- What is persisted from a single user session (requests, intermediate streamed tokens, final generated output, tool outputs, attachments)?
- Residency: where the stored items live (region/replication) by default?
- Deletion timeline and evidence: how long are items retained, and how can we get proof of erasure if requested?

For context, we stream tokens to the client for latency reasons and some workflows use tool calls that output files (e.g., extracted invoices). Please include examples (short) we can show the board.

Thanks — really appreciate a concise, example-driven answer.

—Laura
Security & Privacy Lead
AtlasPay

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chang <laura.chang@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify data lifecycle for interactive sessions & exported artifacts

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear list of asks. Below is a compact, example-led summary you can share with the board; I call out defaults for the Hosted API and notes about Dedicated/Private options where you can change behavior.

1) What we persist by default (Hosted API):
- Request metadata: request ID, client API key hash, timestamp, route/model used — retained for 60 days by default for billing, abuse detection, and quality monitoring.
- Final generated outputs (the finalized text or structured result returned to the client): retained for 60 days by default. This includes outputs that are written to the response stream once the model has completed and the server marks the response as finalized.
- Intermediate streamed tokens: transient. Tokens emitted during streaming are not written to the long-term store by default; they are buffered in-memory and in ephemeral runtime caches tied to the session lifecycle (typical TTL: 30–90 minutes).
- Tool outputs / attachments created by Redwood-integrated tools: treated as artifacts. By default, if a tool call writes an attachment to the response (e.g., invoice.pdf produced by an extraction tool), that artifact is stored in object storage and follows the same 60-day artifact horizon unless you enable a different retention setting.
- KV cache and session context (runtime-only): ephemeral — retained only for the session window to support continuation and performance; default eviction within 1 hour after session inactivity. These are not surfaced in the standard long-term logs.
- Embeddings / indexes: not stored unless explicitly requested (e.g., embeddings API or model upload); if you opt in, those are stored according to the customer-configured index retention policy.

Example 1 — simple chat session:
- User sends prompt -> tokens streamed -> final assistant answer returned. What is kept: request metadata + final answer (60 days). Streamed tokens not persisted.

Example 2 — extraction tool that produces invoice.pdf:
- Tool run produces invoice.pdf attached to the response. What is kept: request metadata + final generated output + artifact invoice.pdf (artifact retention 60 days by default).

2) Residency by default:
- Hosted API: data persists in the region of the request/endpoint (e.g., us-west for US customers) with replication for durability within that region. We do not automatically replicate cross-region unless you enable global replication or Dedicated/Private with cross-region routing.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: residency is customer-configurable (VPC/On‑prem options available).

3) Deletion timeline and evidence:
- Default timeline: retained 60 days (requests + final outputs + artifacts) unless you request a shorter horizon or use a Private deployment.
- Immediate deletion/erasure request: we can schedule targeted erasure for a customer identifier. Erasure jobs may take up to 72 hours to execute across stores and index backfills; we provide an erasure report afterwards with job id and timestamps.
- Proof-of-deletion: for customers on enterprise support / Dedicated, we provide deletion evidence (S3 object tombstones + audit log entries) and a signed attestation on request. For Hosted API self-serve customers we provide a deletion confirmation and log of the erasure job.

Notes & action items:
- If you need default horizons below 60 days (e.g., 30 days) or want artifacts excluded from default capture, we can add that as a specific contract appendix or move you to a Dedicated instance where controls are more granular.
- I attached a short one-page summary (redwood-policy-summary.pdf) and a draft retention matrix (retention_matrix_draft.xlsx) to make this concrete.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to run through a few board questions.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chang <laura.chang@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2029-10-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify data lifecycle for interactive sessions & exported artifacts

Quick notes / suggested wording tweaks for the board: 
- Replace "final generated outputs" with "finalized response payloads" to avoid ambiguity with in-flight artifacts.
- Add a short callout that streaming buffers are never written to persistent object storage unless a customer explicitly requests session transcripts be exported.
- Expand the erasure evidence line: include the types of evidence (audit entry id, object tombstone id, and service-level trace id) so compliance teams know what to expect.

Also: Marissa — can you attach the retention_matrix_draft.xlsx with the column headers we discussed (ArtifactType | DefaultHorizon | StorageLocation | ErasureProcess | EvidenceTypes) before we send a final version to Laura? I left a couple of example rows in the sheet.

-Karthik
Head of Product (Serving)

From: Laura Chang <laura.chang@atlaspay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-19T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify data lifecycle for interactive sessions & exported artifacts

Hannah / team —

This is exactly what we needed, thanks. The examples are helpful and the 60-day default is reasonable for our board, though we may ask for a 30-day horizon in the contract appendix. Please send the finalized one-pager and the retention matrix (with Karthik's evidence column) and we can move to a DocuSign annex to capture any changes.

Two quick asks:
- Can you include a sample erasure report (sanitized) in the retention_matrix_draft.xlsx so our auditors see the format?
- Could Redwood confirm whether artifacts produced by third-party tool integrations (e.g., a partner OCR service) are treated the same as Redwood-produced attachments for retention purposes?

If you confirm both, I'll shepherd this for our legal/compliance reviews.

Thanks again,
—Laura
